title.zh: 卷340 列傳一百二十七 王杰 董诰 朱珪
title.en: Volume 340 Biographies 127: Wang Jie, Dong Gao, Zhu Gui
title.raw: 卷340 列傳一百二十七 王杰 董诰 朱珪

sentences.zh: 王杰，字偉人，陝西韓城人。

translations.literal: Wang Jie, styled Wei Ren, was a man of Hancheng in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie, whose courtesy name was Wei Ren, came from Hancheng in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 以拔貢考銓藍田教諭，未任，遭父喪，貧甚，為書記以養母。

translations.literal: Having passed the examination for tribute-student selection, he was qualified for appointment as Lantian district instructor; before taking office he suffered his father's death; being extremely poor, he served as a secretary to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a tribute student through examination, he was slated to become district instructor in Lantian, but before he could take up the post his father died. Utterly destitute, he earned his living as a secretary to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 歷佐兩江總督尹繼善、江蘇巡撫陳宏謀幕，皆重之。

translations.literal: He successively assisted in the staffs of the Liangjiang governor-general Yin Jishan and the Jiangsu governor Chen Hongmou, and both held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn on the staffs of Liangjiang governor-general Yin Jishan and Jiangsu governor Chen Hongmou, and both men valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 初從武功孫景烈遊，講濂、洛、關、閩之學；

translations.literal: At first he followed Sun Jinglie of Wugong in study, expounding the learning of the Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min schools;
translations.idiomatic: He had first studied under Sun Jinglie of Wugong, immersing himself in the Neo-Confucian traditions associated with Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi;

sentences.zh: 及見宏謀，學益進，自謂生平行己居官得力於此。

translations.literal: when he met Hongmou his learning advanced further, and he said himself that in his conduct through life and in holding office he owed his strength to this.
translations.idiomatic: and after he came under Chen Hongmou's influence his scholarship advanced still further. He later said that his personal conduct and his success in office owed everything to this training.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十六年，成進士，殿試進呈卷列第三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi; on the palace examination his submitted paper ranked third.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign (1761), he passed the metropolitan examination; his palace examination paper was initially ranked third.

sentences.zh: 高宗熟視字體如素識，以昔為尹繼善繕疏，曾邀宸賞，詢知人品，即拔置第一。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor scrutinized the handwriting as if he had known it before; because in the past he had copied memorials for Yin Jishan and had once won imperial praise, he inquired into the man's character and immediately elevated him to first place.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor studied the calligraphy as though it were already familiar to him. Recognizing the hand of the man who had once copied memorials for Yin Jishan and won imperial commendation, he inquired into the candidate's character and at once placed him first.

sentences.zh: 及引見，風度凝然，上益喜。

translations.literal: When he was presented at court, his bearing was composed and dignified, and the emperor was all the more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience his bearing was grave and composed, which pleased the emperor still more.

sentences.zh: 又以陝人入本朝百餘年無大魁者，時值西陲戡定，魁選適得西人，御製詩以紀其事。

translations.literal: Moreover, because for more than a hundred years since the dynasty's founding no Shaanxi native had won the top degree, and at the time the western frontier had just been pacified, the top selection happened to fall to a westerner—the emperor composed an imperial poem to commemorate the event.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, no native of Shaanxi had won first place in the examinations in the dynasty's first century and more; the western borderlands had just been pacified, and the top graduate happened to be a man from the west. The emperor wrote an imperial poem to mark the occasion.

sentences.zh: 尋直南書房，屢司文柄。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was assigned to the Southern Study, and repeatedly held charge of literary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to the Southern Study and repeatedly held authority over literary matters and examinations.

sentences.zh: 五遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he rose to Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，授刑部侍郎，調吏部，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year (1774) he was appointed vice minister of punishments, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，丁母憂，即家擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he entered mourning for his mother; while still at home he was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year (1783) he entered mourning for his mother; while still at home he was promoted to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 車駕南巡，傑赴行在謝，上曰：「汝來甚好。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured the south, Jie went to the traveling palace to give thanks; the emperor said: "Your coming is very good.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the south, Jie went to the traveling palace to offer thanks. The emperor said, "It is very good that you have come.

sentences.zh: 君臣久別，應知朕念汝。

translations.literal: Monarch and minister have long been parted—you should know that I think of you.
translations.idiomatic: Monarch and minister have been apart so long—you must know that I have been thinking of you.

sentences.zh: 然汝儒者，不欲奪汝情，歸終制可也。

translations.literal: Yet you are a Confucian scholar; I do not wish to deprive you of your feelings—return and complete your mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are a Confucian scholar, and I do not wish to deprive you of filial duty. Go home and complete your mourning.

sentences.zh: 」服闋，還朝。

translations.literal: " When the mourning period ended, he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: " When his mourning ended, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，命為軍機大臣、上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was appointed Grand Councilor and Chief Tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year (1786) he was appointed grand councilor and chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 次年，拜東閣大學士，管理禮部。

translations.literal: The following year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and placed in charge of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and put in charge of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 台灣、廓爾喀先後平，兩次圖形紫光閣，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Taiwan and Gurkha were pacified in succession; twice his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan and the Gurkha campaign were pacified in turn, his portrait was twice placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he received the additional title of junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 傑在樞廷十餘年，事有可否，未嘗不委曲陳奏。

translations.literal: Jie was in the Grand Council for more than ten years; whenever a matter was feasible or not, he never failed to set forth his views in full.
translations.idiomatic: Jie served on the Grand Council for more than ten years. On every matter, whether he approved or not, he always presented his views fully and without reserve.

sentences.zh: 和珅勢方赫，事多擅決，同列隱忍不言，傑遇有不可，輒力爭。

translations.literal: Heshen's power was then at its height; he decided many matters on his own authority, and his colleagues endured in silence, but whenever Jie found something unacceptable he would contend vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen's power was then at its height; he decided many matters on his own, and his colleagues endured in silence. Whenever Jie found something unacceptable, however, he argued vigorously.

sentences.zh: 上知之深，和珅雖厭之而不能去。

translations.literal: The emperor knew him deeply; although Heshen detested him, he could not remove him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew him well. Heshen detested him but could not remove him.

sentences.zh: 傑每議政畢，默然獨坐。

translations.literal: Whenever Jie finished discussing policy, he would sit alone in silence.
translations.idiomatic: After each policy discussion Jie would sit apart in silence.

sentences.zh: 一日，和珅執其手戲曰：「何柔荑乃爾！

translations.literal: One day Heshen took his hand in jest and said: "How soft and delicate they are!
translations.idiomatic: One day Heshen took his hand playfully and said, "How soft and delicate your hands are!

sentences.zh: 」傑正色曰：「王杰手雖好，但不能要錢耳！

translations.literal: " Jie said sternly: "Wang Jie's hands may be fine, but they cannot take money!
translations.idiomatic: " Jie replied sternly, "Wang Jie's hands may be fine, but they will not take money!

sentences.zh: 」和珅赧然。

translations.literal: " Heshen flushed with embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: " Heshen flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，以足疾乞免軍機、書房及管理部事，允之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, on account of foot ailment he begged to be relieved of Grand Council duties, the Study, and departmental administration; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing (1796), citing foot ailment, he asked to be relieved of his posts on the Grand Council, in the Study, and in departmental administration; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 有大事，上必諮詢，傑亦不時入告。

translations.literal: When major affairs arose the emperor was sure to consult him, and Jie also entered from time to time to report.
translations.idiomatic: On major affairs the emperor still consulted him, and Jie also came in from time to time to advise.

sentences.zh: 時教匪方熾，傑疏言：「賊匪剿滅稽遲，由被賊災民窮無倚賴，地方官不能勞來安輯，以致脅從日眾，兵力日單而賊焰日熾。

translations.literal: At the time the sect rebels were raging; Jie memorialized, saying: "The delay in exterminating the bandits stems from the fact that the people afflicted by the rebels are destitute and without support, and local officials cannot comfort and settle them, so that those compelled to follow grow daily in number, military strength daily grows thin, and rebel flames daily blaze higher.
translations.idiomatic: The White Lotus rebellion was then at its height. Jie submitted a memorial saying, "The delay in suppressing the rebels stems from the destitution of people in rebel-afflicted areas, whom local officials fail to comfort and resettle. Compelled followers grow daily in number while government forces dwindle and rebel strength mounts.

sentences.zh: 此時當安良民以解從賊之心，撫官兵以勵行間之氣。

translations.literal: At this time one should settle the good people to dissolve the hearts of those following the rebels, and comfort the officers and soldiers to encourage morale in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The urgent need is to reassure law-abiding subjects so as to loosen rebel ranks, and to support officers and soldiers so as to restore fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 三年之內，川、楚、秦、豫四省殺傷不下數百萬，其倖存而不從賊者，亦皆鋒鏑之餘，男不暇耕，女不暇織。

translations.literal: Within three years in the four provinces of Sichuan, Huguang, Shaanxi, and Henan the killed and wounded were no fewer than several millions; even those who survived and did not follow the rebels were all remnants after battle—men had no leisure to plow, women no leisure to weave.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years the four provinces of Sichuan, Huguang, Shaanxi, and Henan had suffered millions of casualties. Even survivors who had not joined the rebels were left shattered by war—men could not plow, women could not weave.

sentences.zh: 若再計畝徵輸，甚至分外加派，胥吏因緣勒索，艱苦情形無由上達聖主之前。

translations.literal: If on top of this grain tax is levied by the mu and even extra assessments are imposed, and clerks seize the opportunity to extort, the bitter circumstances cannot reach the sage ruler.
translations.idiomatic: If taxes are levied acre by acre, with extra surcharges on top, and clerks extort at every turn, their suffering will never reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 祈將被賊地方錢糧蠲免，不令官吏舞弊重徵，有來歸者概勿窮治，賊勢或可漸孤矣。

translations.literal: I pray that grain taxes in rebel-afflicted places be remitted, that officials not be allowed to cheat and levy heavily, and that those who return be altogether not prosecuted to the end—then rebel strength may gradually be isolated.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that taxes in rebel-afflicted regions be remitted, that officials be barred from fraudulent over-collection, and that returning subjects not be prosecuted—so that rebel strength may gradually be isolated.

sentences.zh: 至於用兵三載未即成功，實由將帥有所依恃，怠玩因循，非盡士卒之不用命也。

translations.literal: As for three years of campaigning without immediate success, this truly stems from generals having something to rely on, being negligent and procrastinating—it is not wholly that the soldiers refuse to obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: As for three years of war without decisive victory, the real cause is that commanders, secure in their positions, have grown negligent and procrastinating. It is not simply that the troops refuse to fight.

sentences.zh: 乞頒發諭旨，曲加憐恤，有驕惰不馴者，令經略概行撤回，或就近更調召募，申明紀律，鼓行勵戎，庶幾人有挾纊之歡，眾有成城之志。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be issued showing special compassion; those who are arrogant, lazy, and unruly should be recalled wholesale by the commander, or replaced and recruited nearby; discipline should be declared, troops encouraged to advance—then perhaps each man will have the joy of having a quilt in winter, and all will have the will to defend the city together.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that an edict issue showing special compassion: arrogant and undisciplined officers should be recalled by the commander, or replaced with local recruits; discipline should be enforced and the army urged forward—so that the troops may feel cared for and the whole force regain the will to stand firm together.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「教匪之蔓延，其弊有二：一由統領之有名無實。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The spread of the sect rebels has two abuses: one is that the commander-in-chief is nominal without reality.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote, "The spread of the sect rebels has two root causes. The first is that the supreme commander is nominal only.

sentences.zh: 勒保雖為統領，而統兵大員名位相等，人人得專摺奏事，於是賊至則畏避不前，賊去則捏稱得勝。

translations.literal: Although Lebao is commander-in-chief, the officers commanding troops are equal in rank and title, and each may submit memorials on his own; thus when rebels arrive they shrink back and do not advance, and when rebels leave they fabricate claims of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Although Lebao is commander-in-chief, the field commanders are his equals in rank, and each may submit memorials independently. When rebels appear they hang back; when rebels withdraw they claim victories they never fought.

sentences.zh: 即如前歲賊竄興安，領兵大員有'匪已渡江五日，地方官並不禀報'之奏，此其畏避情形顯而易見。

translations.literal: For example, the year before last when rebels fled into Xing'an, a commanding officer memorialized that 'the bandits had crossed the river five days ago and the local officials had not reported'—this shows their shrinking back clearly.
translations.idiomatic: The year before last, when rebels raided Xing'an, one commander reported that the bandits had crossed the river five days earlier while local officials had not reported at all—a clear sign of cowardice.

sentences.zh: 又如去歲賊擾西安城南，殺傷數万，官兵既不近賊，撫臣一無設施；

translations.literal: Again, last year when rebels harassed south of Xi'an city, tens of thousands were killed and wounded; the officers and soldiers neither approached the rebels, and the governor did nothing at all;
translations.idiomatic: Again, last year when rebels struck south of Xi'an, tens of thousands were killed or wounded. The troops never closed with the enemy, and the governor took no effective measures;

sentences.zh: 探知賊去已遠，然後虛張聲勢，名為追賊，實未見賊。

translations.literal: only after learning the rebels had gone far away did they make a false show of force, calling it pursuit of rebels when in fact they had not seen rebels.
translations.idiomatic: only after learning the rebels were far away did they stage a show of pursuit—naming it pursuit when they had never seen the enemy.

sentences.zh: 近聞張漢潮蔓延商、雒，高均德屯據洋縣，往來衝突，如入無人之境。

translations.literal: Recently it is heard that Zhang Hanchao spreads through Shang and Luo, Gao Junde occupies Yang County, coming and going in collision as if entering a land with no one in it.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Zhang Hanchao has spread through Shangzhou and Luozhou, and Gao Junde has occupied Yang County, raiding back and forth as though no one opposed them.

sentences.zh: 秦省如此，川省可知。

translations.literal: If Shaanxi is thus, Sichuan may be known.
translations.idiomatic: If Shaanxi is in this state, Sichuan may be imagined.

sentences.zh: 實由統領不專、賞罰不明之所致也。

translations.literal: This truly stems from the commander-in-chief not having sole authority and rewards and punishments not being clear.
translations.idiomatic: This truly stems from divided command and unclear rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 一由領兵大員專恃鄉勇。

translations.literal: The second is that commanding officers rely solely on local militia.
translations.idiomatic: The second is that field commanders rely solely on local militia.

sentences.zh: 鄉勇陣亡，無庸報部，人數可以虛捏；

translations.literal: When militia die in battle there is no need to report to the ministry, and numbers may be fabricated;
translations.idiomatic: Militia casualties need not be reported to the ministry, and numbers may be invented;

sentences.zh: 藉鄉勇為前陣，既可免官兵之傷亡，又可為異日之開銷，此所以耗國帑而無可稽核也。

translations.literal: using militia as the front line both spares regular troops from casualties and provides future expenses—this is why state funds are drained with nothing to audit.
translations.idiomatic: using militia as the front line spares regular troops and pads future expense accounts—hence the drain on the treasury with nothing to audit.

sentences.zh: 臣以為軍務緊要，莫急於去鄉勇之名而為召募之實，蓋有五利：一，民窮無依，多半從賊，苟延性命，募而為兵，即有口糧，多一為兵之人，即少一從賊之人；

translations.literal: Your subject considers that in military affairs nothing is more urgent than removing the name of militia and making recruitment real; there are five advantages: first, the people are destitute and without support, and mostly follow the rebels to prolong life—if recruited as soldiers they have rations; each man who becomes a soldier is one fewer who follows the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that nothing in the war effort is more urgent than ending the militia fiction and recruiting real soldiers. There are five advantages. First, destitute people with nowhere to turn mostly join the rebels to survive; recruited as soldiers they receive rations—each new soldier is one fewer rebel follower;

sentences.zh: 一，隔省徵調，曠日持久，就近召募，則旬日可得；

translations.literal: second, calling troops from other provinces takes long days; recruiting nearby can be done in ten days;
translations.idiomatic: second, calling troops from distant provinces takes months, whereas local recruitment can be completed in ten days;

sentences.zh: 一，徵兵遠來，筋力已疲，召募之人，不須跋涉；

translations.literal: third, troops called from afar are already weary in sinew and strength; recruited men need not travel far;
translations.idiomatic: third, troops summoned from afar arrive exhausted, whereas recruits need not make long marches;

sentences.zh: 一，隔省之兵，水土不習，路徑不諳，就近之人，則不慮此；

translations.literal: fourth, troops from other provinces are unaccustomed to water and soil and unfamiliar with paths; men nearby need not fear this;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, troops from other provinces are unaccustomed to climate and terrain, whereas local men are not;

sentences.zh: 一，鄉勇勢不能敵，則逃散無從懲治，召募之兵退避，則有軍法。

translations.literal: fifth, when militia cannot match the enemy they scatter and flee with no means of punishment, but when recruited troops retreat there is military law.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, when militia cannot stand they scatter without penalty, but regular recruits who retreat face military law.

sentences.zh: 具此五利，何不增募，一鼓而殲賊？

translations.literal: With these five advantages, why not increase recruitment and destroy the rebels in one stroke?
translations.idiomatic: With these five advantages, why not expand recruitment and crush the rebels in one campaign?

sentences.zh: 如謂兵多費多，獨不思一萬兵食十月之糧，與十萬兵食一月之糧，其費相等而功可早奏也。

translations.literal: If one says many troops mean great expense, does one alone not consider that ten thousand troops eating ten months' grain and one hundred thousand troops eating one month's grain cost the same while success can be reported early?
translations.idiomatic: If the objection is that more troops mean more expense, has one not considered that ten thousand men fed for ten months costs the same as one hundred thousand fed for one month, while victory may be won far sooner?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，並被採用。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, both points were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the throne, both recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 二年，復召直軍機，隨扈熱河。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again summoned to attend the Grand Council and accompanied the entourage to Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1797) he was again summoned to the Grand Council and accompanied the court to Rehe.

sentences.zh: 未幾，因腿疾，詔毋庸入直，先行回京。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of leg ailment, an edict said he need not attend duty; he returned first to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, citing leg ailment, he was excused from attendance and returned to Beijing ahead of the court.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，川匪王三槐就擒，封賞樞臣，詔：「傑現雖未直軍機，軍興曾有贊畫功，並予優敘。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year the Sichuan rebel Wang Sanhuai was captured; rewards were given to Grand Council members; an edict said: "Although Jie is not now attending the Grand Council, in the military rise he once had merit in planning, and he is also to receive preferential treatment.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year (1798), the Sichuan rebel Wang Sanhuai was captured. The grand councilors were rewarded, and an edict read, "Although Jie is not currently on the Grand Council, he contributed to planning during the war and shall receive preferential recognition as well.

sentences.zh: 洎仁宗親政，傑為首輔，遇事持大體，竭誠進諫，上優禮之。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor personally took power, Jie was chief minister; in handling affairs he upheld the larger pattern, exhaustively remonstrating, and the emperor treated him with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiaqing Emperor took personal control of government, Jie became chief minister. He upheld broad principles, remonstrated with full sincerity, and the emperor treated him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 五年，以衰病乞休，溫詔慰留，許扶杖入朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on account of decline and illness he begged to retire; a warm edict comforted him and kept him, permitting him to enter court leaning on a staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1800), citing age and illness, he asked to retire. A warm edict urged him to stay and allowed him to attend court leaning on a staff.

sentences.zh: 七年，固請致仕，晉太子太傅，在籍食俸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he firmly requested retirement; he was advanced to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and received salary while at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1802) he firmly requested retirement and was promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent, retaining his salary in his native place.

sentences.zh: 八年春，瀕行上疏，略謂：「各省虧空之弊，起於乾隆四十年以後，州縣營求餽送，以國帑為夤緣，上司受其挾制，彌補無期。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, on the eve of departure he memorialized, saying in summary: "The abuse of provincial deficits began after the fortieth year of Qianlong; districts and counties sought gifts and presents, using state funds as a ladder of connection; superiors were constrained by them, and there was no end to making up deficits.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year (1803), on the eve of his departure he submitted a memorial summarizing his views: "Provincial deficits began after the fortieth year of Qianlong. District and county officials courted superiors with gifts, treating the public purse as a ladder of patronage; their superiors were held hostage, and deficits could never be made good.

sentences.zh: 至嘉慶四年以後，大吏知尚廉節，州縣仍形拮据，由於苦樂不均，賢否不分，宜求整飭之法。

translations.literal: After the fourth year of Jiaqing, high officials knew to value integrity, yet districts and counties still showed strain, because joy and suffering were unevenly distributed and the worthy and unworthy were not distinguished—methods of rectification should be sought.
translations.idiomatic: After the fourth year of Jiaqing, senior officials valued integrity, yet local officials remained strained—because hardship and ease were unevenly distributed and the worthy could not be told from the unworthy. Methods of rectification must be found.

sentences.zh: 又，舊制，驛丞專司驛站，無可誅求。

translations.literal: Moreover, under the old system the post-station superintendent had sole charge of post stations and there was nothing to demand.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, post-station superintendents managed the stations alone, leaving no room for extortion.

sentences.zh: 自裁歸州縣，濫支苛派，官民俱病。

translations.literal: Since the post was abolished and returned to districts and counties, expenditures were abused and levies were harsh; officials and people alike suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Since the post was abolished and its duties assigned to district and county governments, expenses have been abused and levies harsh—officials and common people alike suffer.

sentences.zh: 宜先清驛站，以杜虧空。

translations.literal: Post stations should first be cleared up to stop deficits.
translations.idiomatic: Post stations should be put in order first, to stop the drain of deficits.

sentences.zh: 今當軍務告竣，朝廷勤求治理，無大於此二者。

translations.literal: Now that military affairs are concluded, the court is diligently seeking good government—nothing is greater than these two matters.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the war is over and the court is earnestly seeking good government, nothing is more important than these two reforms.

sentences.zh: 請睿裁獨斷，以挽積重之勢。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty for wise decision alone, to reverse the weight of long accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide alone and reverse these deeply entrenched abuses.

sentences.zh: 」所言切中時弊，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: " What he said struck the abuses of the time; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " His words struck at the abuses of the day, and the emperor praised and accepted them.

sentences.zh: 陛辭日，賜高宗御用玉鳩杖、御製詩二章，以寵其行，有云：「直道一身立廊廟，清風兩袖返韓城。

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience he was given the Gaozong Emperor's personal jade dove staff and two chapters of imperial composition to honor his departure, with the lines: "Upright in body he stood in the hall of state; with clear wind and empty sleeves he returns to Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his farewell audience the emperor gave him the Qianlong Emperor's personal jade dove staff and two imperial poems to honor his departure, including the lines, "Upright in body he stood in the hall of state; with clear wind and empty sleeves he returns to Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 」時論謂足盡其生平。

translations.literal: " Contemporary opinion said this fully summed up his life.
translations.idiomatic: " Contemporary opinion held that these lines summed up his life.

sentences.zh: 既歸，歲時頒賞不絕，每有陳奏，上輒親批答，語如家人。

translations.literal: After he returned, seasonal bestowals never ceased; whenever he memorialized, the emperor personally wrote replies in a tone like family.
translations.idiomatic: After his return, seasonal gifts from the throne never ceased. Whenever he submitted a memorial, the emperor answered in his own hand, in a tone like that between family members.

sentences.zh: 九年，傑與妻程並年八十，命巡撫方維甸齎御​​製詩、額、珍物，於生日就賜其家。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Jie and his wife Cheng were both eighty; he ordered the governor Fang Weidian to bring imperial poems, a plaque, and precious objects and bestow them at their home on their birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1804), Jie and his wife née Cheng both turned eighty. The emperor ordered Governor Fang Weidian to bring imperial poems, a plaque, and precious gifts and present them at their home on their birthday.

sentences.zh: 傑詣闕謝，明年正月，卒於京邸。

translations.literal: Jie went to the palace to give thanks; in the first month of the following year he died at his Beijing residence.
translations.idiomatic: Jie went to the palace to give thanks. In the first month of the following year he died at his Beijing residence.

sentences.zh: 上悼惜，賜金治喪，贈太子太師，祀賢良祠，諡文端。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him, gave gold for the funeral, posthumously appointed him Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, and gave the posthumous title Wénduān.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, granted gold for the funeral, posthumously appointed him senior tutor of the heir apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthy Ministers, and gave him the posthumous title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 傑體不逾中人，和靄近情，而持守剛正，歷事兩朝，以忠直結主知。

translations.literal: Jie's physique did not exceed medium height; he was genial and approachable, yet upheld stern integrity; serving two reigns, he won the ruler's trust through loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was of no more than medium height, genial and approachable, yet steadfastly upright. Serving two reigns, he won the emperor's trust through loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 當致仕未行，會有陳德於禁城驚犯乘輿，急趨朝請對曰：「德庖廚賤役，安敢妄蓄逆謀？

translations.literal: When he had requested retirement but not yet departed, there occurred the case of Chen De startling the imperial carriage within the Forbidden City; he hurried to court and requested an audience, saying: "De is a low kitchen servant—how dare he harbor rebellious designs?
translations.idiomatic: When he had requested retirement but not yet left the capital, Chen De alarmed the imperial carriage within the Forbidden City. Jie hurried to court and requested an audience, saying, "Chen De is a lowly kitchen servant—how could he harbor treasonous designs on his own?

sentences.zh: 此必有元姦大憝主使行明張差之事，當除肘腋之患。

translations.literal: There must be a chief villain and great criminal master-minding an affair like the Ming Zhang Cha affair—the trouble at the elbow and armpit should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: There must be a powerful villain behind him, orchestrating something like the Zhang Cha affair of the Ming dynasty. The danger at the emperor's very side must be removed.

sentences.zh: 」至十八年林清逆黨之變，上思其言，特賜祭焉。

translations.literal: " When in the eighteenth year the Lin Qing rebel faction rose, the emperor recalled his words and specially sent sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Lin Qing conspiracy erupted in the eighteenth year (1813), the emperor recalled his words and specially sent offerings to his spirit.

sentences.zh: 孫篤，道光二年進士，歷編修、御史，出為汀州知府、廣東督糧道，署鹽運使。

translations.literal: His grandson Du, a jinshi in the second year of Daoguang, successively served as compiler and censor, and went out as prefect of Tingzhou, Guangdong grain transport commissioner, and acting salt controller.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Du, a jinshi of the second Daoguang year (1822), served as compiler and censor, then as prefect of Tingzhou, Guangdong grain transport commissioner, and acting salt controller.

sentences.zh: 時林則徐為按察使，治海防，甚倚之。

translations.literal: At the time Lin Zexu was provincial judge, managing coastal defense, and relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lin Zexu was provincial judge in charge of coastal defense and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 募廣州遊手精壯者備守禦，以機敏稱。

translations.literal: He recruited sturdy men among Guangzhou idlers for defense, and was known for quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited sturdy Guangzhou idlers for coastal defense and was known for resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 擢山東布政使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Shandong provincial administration commissioner and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Shandong provincial administration commissioner and acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 失察家人、屬官受賂，連降罷職歸，襄理西安城工。

translations.literal: For failure to supervise his household and subordinate officials accepting bribes, he was demoted in succession, dismissed, and returned home to assist in managing Xi'an city works.
translations.idiomatic: For failing to prevent his household and subordinates from taking bribes, he was repeatedly demoted, dismissed, and sent home to help manage the Xi'an city reconstruction.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈布政使銜。

translations.literal: When he died he was given the posthumous rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was granted the posthumous rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 董誥，字蔗林，浙江富陽人，尚書邦達子。

translations.literal: Dong Gao, styled Zhelín, was a man of Fuyang in Zhejiang, son of Minister Dong Bangda.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Gao, whose courtesy name was Zhelín, came from Fuyang in Zhejiang. He was the son of Minister Dong Bangda.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十八年進士，殿試進呈卷列第三，高宗因大臣子，改二甲第一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi; on the palace examination his submitted paper ranked third; because he was a minister's son the Gaozong Emperor changed him to first in the second class.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong (1763) he passed the metropolitan examination. His palace examination paper ranked third, but because he was a minister's son the emperor placed him first in the second class.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，即預修國史、三通、皇朝禮器圖。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he at once took part in compiling the National History, the Three Comprehensive Works, and the Imperial Rites Implements Illustrated.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he at once joined the compilation of the National History, the Three Comprehensive Works, and the Illustrated Imperial Rites Implements.

sentences.zh: 散館，授編修。

translations.literal: When the bachelors were released from the Academy he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When his term in the Academy ended, he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，命入懋勤殿寫金字經為皇太后祝嘏。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was ordered to enter the Hall of Military Glory to copy the gold-letter sutra for the empress dowager's birthday blessing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year (1767) he was ordered to the Hall of Military Glory to copy the gold-letter sutra for the empress dowager's birthday blessing.

sentences.zh: 次年，大考翰詹，因寫經未與試，特加一級。

translations.literal: The following year, in the great examination of Hanlin and Academy members, because he was copying sutras he did not take the test and was specially given one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the triennial examination of Hanlin and Academy members, he was excused because of sutra copying and was specially advanced one rank.

sentences.zh: 尋擢中允，丁父憂。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to junior expositor and entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to junior expositor, then entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，服闋，入直南書房。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, when mourning ended, he entered the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year (1771), when his mourning ended, he was assigned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 初，邦達善畫，受高宗知。

translations.literal: At first Bangda was skilled at painting and won the Gaozong Emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bangda had been skilled at painting and won the Qianlong Emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 誥承家學，繼為侍從，書畫亦被宸賞，尤以奉職恪勤為上所眷注。

translations.literal: Gao inherited the family learning, continued as attendant, and his painting and calligraphy also won imperial praise; especially because of dutiful service he was the object of the emperor's special regard.
translations.idiomatic: Gao inherited the family craft, served as an attendant, and his painting and calligraphy also won imperial praise; above all, his dutiful service won the emperor's special regard.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to grand secretary of the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 四十年，擢工部侍郎，調戶部，歷署吏、刑兩部侍郎，兼管樂部。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works, transferred to Revenue, and successively acted as Vice Minister of Personnel and Punishments, while also managing the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year (1775) he was promoted to vice minister of works, transferred to revenue, and in turn acted as vice minister of personnel and punishments while also managing the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 充四庫館副總裁，接辦全書薈要，命輯滿洲源流考。

translations.literal: He served as deputy director of the Siku Library, took over compilation of the Essentials of the Complete Library, and was ordered to compile the Origins of the Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy director of the Siku Library, took charge of the Essentials of the Complete Library, and was ordered to compile the Origins of the Manchus.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year (1779) he was appointed grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，加太子少保，擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year (1787) he received the additional title of junior guardian of the heir apparent and was promoted to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 台灣、廓爾喀先後底定，並列功臣，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: Taiwan and Gurkha were successively settled; he was listed among the meritorious ministers and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan and the Gurkha campaign were pacified in turn, he was listed among the meritorious ministers and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，授受禮成，詔硃珪來京，將畀以閣務，仁宗賀以詩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, when the succession ceremony was completed, an edict summoned Zhu Gui to the capital to be given Grand Secretariat duties; the Renzong Emperor congratulated him with a poem.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing (1796), when the succession ceremony was completed, an edict summoned Zhu Gui to the capital to receive a grand secretariat appointment; the Jiaqing Emperor congratulated him with a poem.

sentences.zh: 屬稿未竟，和珅取白高宗曰：「嗣皇帝欲市恩於師傅。

translations.literal: The draft was not yet finished when Heshen reported to the Gaozong Emperor, saying: "The heir apparent wishes to curry favor with his tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Before the draft was finished, Heshen reported to the Qianlong Emperor, "The heir apparent wishes to curry favor with his tutor.

sentences.zh: 」高宗色動，顧誥曰：「汝在軍機、刑部久，是於律意云何？

translations.literal: " The Gaozong Emperor's expression changed; he turned to Gao and said: "You have long been in the Grand Council and the Ministry of Punishments—what is your view of the intent of the law?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's expression changed. He turned to Gao and said, "You have long served on the Grand Council and at the Ministry of Punishments—what is your view of the law in this matter?

sentences.zh: 」誥叩頭曰：「聖主無過言。

translations.literal: " Gao kowtowed and said: "The sage ruler's words are without fault.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao kowtowed and said, "The sage ruler's words are without fault.

sentences.zh: 」高宗默然良久，曰：「汝大臣也，善為朕輔導之。

translations.literal: " The Gaozong Emperor was silent a long while, then said: "You are a great minister—well guide him for Us.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was silent a long while, then said, "You are a great minister—guide him well for me.

sentences.zh: 」乃以他事罷珪之召。

translations.literal: " Thereupon on another pretext Zhu Gui's summons was cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon, on another pretext, Zhu Gui's summons was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 時大學士懸缺久，難其人。

translations.literal: At the time the post of grand secretary had long been vacant, and a suitable man was hard to find.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretary post had long been vacant, and a suitable appointee was hard to find.

sentences.zh: 高宗謂劉墉、紀昀、彭元瑞三人皆資深，墉遇事模棱，元瑞以不檢獲愆，昀讀書多而不明理，惟誥在直勤勉，超拜東閣大學士，明詔宣示，俾三人加愧勵焉。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor said that Liu Yong, Ji Yun, and Peng Yuanrui were all senior in standing: Liu was evasive in handling affairs, Peng had been censured for lack of restraint, and Ji read much but did not understand principle—only Gao was diligent in attendance; he was promoted over the usual steps to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, with an explicit edict proclaiming this to make the three feel shame and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor said that Liu Yong, Ji Yun, and Peng Yuanrui were all senior: Liu was evasive in affairs, Peng had been censured for misconduct, and Ji read widely but lacked practical judgment—only Gao was diligent in attendance. Gao was promoted out of turn to grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, with an explicit edict to shame and spur the other three.

sentences.zh: 命總理禮部，仍兼管戶部事。

translations.literal: He was ordered to take general charge of the Ministry of Rites while still managing Revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take general charge of the Ministry of Rites while still managing revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，丁生母憂，特賜陀羅經被，遣御前侍衛、額駙丰紳殷德奠醊。

translations.literal: In the second year he entered mourning for his birth mother; he was specially given a Dharmakara sutra quilt, and an imperial bodyguard and the imperial son-in-law Fengshen Yinde were sent to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1797) he entered mourning for his birth mother. He was specially given a Dharmakara sutra quilt, and an imperial bodyguard together with the imperial son-in-law Fengshen Yinde were sent to offer libations.

sentences.zh: 誥既以喪歸，川、楚兵事方亟，高宗欲召之，每見大臣，數問；

translations.literal: After Gao had returned home in mourning, military affairs in Sichuan and Huguang were urgent; the Gaozong Emperor wished to summon him and whenever he saw great ministers asked repeatedly;
translations.idiomatic: After Gao returned home in mourning, the war in Sichuan and Huguang was urgent. The Qianlong Emperor wished to recall him and whenever he saw senior ministers asked repeatedly,

sentences.zh: 「董誥何時來？

translations.literal: "When will Dong Gao come?
translations.idiomatic: "When will Dong Gao come?

sentences.zh: 」逾年，葬母畢，詣京師，和珅遏不上聞。

translations.literal: " After more than a year, when his mother's burial was complete, he went to the capital; Heshen blocked the report from reaching the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " After more than a year, when his mother's burial was complete, he went to the capital, but Heshen blocked the report from reaching the throne.

sentences.zh: 會駕出，誥於道旁謝恩，高宗見之，喜甚，命暫署刑部尚書，素服視事，不預典禮，專辦秋讞及軍營紀略，且曰：「誥守制已逾小祥，不得已用人之苦心，眾當共諒。

translations.literal: It happened that the imperial carriage went out; Gao gave thanks for grace by the roadside; the Gaozong Emperor saw him and was greatly pleased, ordering him temporarily to act as Minister of Punishments, wearing plain mourning garb while handling affairs, not participating in ceremonies, devoted to autumn assizes and military camp records, and saying: "Gao's mourning has already passed the first anniversary—Our bitter necessity in using a man should be understood by all.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession went out, Gao gave thanks by the roadside. The emperor saw him and was greatly pleased. He ordered Gao temporarily to act as minister of punishments, wearing plain mourning garb, excused from ceremonies, and devoted to autumn assizes and military records, saying, "Gao's mourning has already passed the first anniversary—my bitter necessity in using him should be understood by all.

sentences.zh: 」尋以王三槐就擒，與軍機大臣同被議敘。

translations.literal: " Soon, because Wang Sanhuai was captured, he received the same preferential treatment as the Grand Council members.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon, when Wang Sanhuai was captured, he received the same preferential treatment as the grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 四年春，高宗崩，和珅伏誅，命誥复直軍機，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the Gaozong Emperor died, Heshen was executed, and Gao was ordered to resume attendance at the Grand Council and advanced to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year (1799) the Qianlong Emperor died and Heshen was executed. Gao was ordered to resume attendance at the Grand Council and was advanced to senior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 既，服闋，授文華殿大學士，兼刑部尚書如故。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory, still concurrently Minister of Punishments as before.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory, still concurrently minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 高宗山陵禮成，命題神主，晉太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor's mausoleum rites were completed he was ordered to compose the spirit tablet and was advanced to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor's mausoleum rites were completed he was ordered to compose the spirit tablet and was advanced to junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 七年，三省教匪平，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the sect rebels in the three provinces were pacified and he was given the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1802) the sect rebels in the three provinces were pacified and he was given the hereditary rank of commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十二年，高宗實錄告成，詔以誥在館八年，始終其事，特加優獎，賜其父邦達入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Veritable Records of the Gaozong Emperor were completed; an edict said that because Gao had been in the library eight years and had seen the work through from start to finish, he received special reward and his father Bangda was granted enshrinement in the Shrine of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1807) the Veritable Records of the Qianlong Emperor were completed. An edict noted that Gao had spent eight years in the library and had seen the work through from start to finish; he received special reward, and his father Bangda was granted enshrinement in the Shrine of Worthy Ministers.

sentences.zh: 十四年，萬壽慶典，晉太子太師。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, at the longevity celebration, he was advanced to Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1809), at the imperial longevity celebration, he was advanced to senior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: He served as Chief Tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 十七年，晉太保。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced to Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1812) he was advanced to grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 十八年，扈從秋狝。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he accompanied the autumn hunt.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1813) he accompanied the autumn hunt.

sentences.zh: 林清逆黨突入禁城，時回鑾，中途聞變，有議俟調大兵成列而後進者，誥曰：「是滋亂也，獻俘者行至矣！

translations.literal: Lin Qing's rebel faction suddenly entered the Forbidden City; at the time the court was returning from the hunt; midway they heard of the disturbance; some proposed waiting until large troops were assembled in formation before advancing; Gao said: "That would only stir disorder—the captives are already on their way!
translations.idiomatic: Lin Qing's rebels suddenly entered the Forbidden City while the court was returning from the hunt. Midway they heard of the disturbance. Some proposed waiting until large bodies of troops were assembled before advancing. Gao said, "That would only stir disorder—the captives are already on their way!

sentences.zh: 」即日扈駕進次，人心乃定。

translations.literal: " That same day he accompanied the carriage to advance to the next stop, and popular feeling was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he accompanied the carriage to the next stop, and public morale was thereby steadied.

sentences.zh: 窮治邪教，誥謂：「燒香祈福，愚民無知，率所常有。

translations.literal: In thoroughly prosecuting the heterodox sects, Gao said: "Burning incense to seek blessing is ignorance among the foolish people and commonly occurs.
translations.idiomatic: In prosecuting the heterodox sects, Gao said, "Burning incense to seek blessings is common ignorance among the people.

sentences.zh: 惟從逆者不可貸。

translations.literal: Only those who followed the rebels must not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Only those who followed the rebels must not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」凡論上，皆以是定讞。

translations.literal: " Whenever cases were submitted for decision, judgments were fixed by this principle.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever cases were submitted, judgments were fixed by this principle.

sentences.zh: 林清既誅，滑縣逆匪尋平，論功，迭被優敘，賜子淳為郎中。

translations.literal: After Lin Qing was executed the rebels in Huaxian County were soon pacified; in assessing merit he was repeatedly given preferential treatment and his son Chun was granted the post of director in a ministry.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin Qing was executed the rebels in Huaxian County were soon pacified. In assessing merit Gao was repeatedly given preferential treatment, and his son Chun was granted a directorship in a ministry.

sentences.zh: 二十年，因病請致政，溫詔慰留，改管兵部。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, on account of illness he requested retirement; a warm edict comforted him and kept him, changing his charge to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1815), citing illness, he requested retirement. A warm edict urged him to stay and transferred his charge to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復命管刑部。

translations.literal: Before long he was again ordered to manage the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again ordered to manage the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，再疏乞休，許致仕食全俸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he again memorialized begging to retire; he was permitted to retire with full salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1818) he again memorialized begging to retire and was permitted to retire on full salary.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，卒，贈太傅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year he died and was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year he died and was posthumously appointed grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 上親奠，入祀賢良祠，賜金治喪，御製詩輓之，嘉其父子歷事三朝，未嘗增置一畝之田、一椽之屋，命刻詩於墓，以彰忠藎。

translations.literal: The emperor personally offered libations, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, gave gold for the funeral, and composed an imperial elegy, praising father and son for serving three reigns without ever adding an extra mu of field or a single rafter of house; he ordered the poem carved on the tomb to manifest loyalty and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally offered libations, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthy Ministers, granted gold for the funeral, and composed an imperial elegy praising father and son for serving three reigns without ever adding an extra mu of land or a single rafter to their house. He ordered the poem carved on the tomb to manifest their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 諡文恭。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Wéngōng.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wengong.

sentences.zh: 誥直軍機先後四十年，熟於朝章故事，有以諮者，無不悉。

translations.literal: Gao attended the Grand Council for forty years in all, was thoroughly versed in court regulations and precedents, and whenever anyone consulted him there was nothing he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Gao served on the Grand Council for forty years in all, was thoroughly versed in court regulations and precedents, and there was nothing he did not know when consulted.

sentences.zh: 凡所獻納皆面陳，未嘗用奏牘。

translations.literal: Whatever he presented he stated in person and never used written memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he presented he stated in person and never used written memorials.

sentences.zh: 當和珅用事，與王杰支柱其間，獨居深念，行處幾失常度，卒贊仁宗殲除大憝。

translations.literal: When Heshen was in power he and Wang Jie supported each other between them; alone he brooded deeply, and in going about he nearly lost his normal composure, yet in the end he assisted the Renzong Emperor in destroying the great villain.
translations.idiomatic: When Heshen was in power he and Wang Jie supported each other. Alone he brooded deeply and in going about nearly lost his composure, yet in the end he assisted the Jiaqing Emperor in destroying the great villain.

sentences.zh: 及林清之變，獨持鎮定，尤為時稱雲。

translations.literal: At the Lin Qing disturbance he alone maintained calm, which contemporaries especially praised.
translations.idiomatic: At the Lin Qing disturbance he alone maintained calm, which contemporaries especially praised.

sentences.zh: 硃珪，字石君，順天大興人。

translations.literal: Zhu Gui, styled Shijun, was a man of Daxing in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui, whose courtesy name was Shijun, came from Daxing in Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先世居蕭山，自父文炳始遷籍。

translations.literal: His forebears lived in Xiaoshan; from his father Wenbing the family changed registration.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had lived in Xiaoshan; his family changed registration beginning with his father Wenbing.

sentences.zh: 文炳官盩厔知縣，曾受經於大學士硃軾。

translations.literal: Wenbing served as magistrate of Zhouzhi and had once received instruction from Grand Secretary Zhu Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing served as magistrate of Zhouzhi and had once studied under Grand Secretary Zhu Shi.

sentences.zh: 珪少傳軾學，與兄筠同鄉舉，並負時譽。

translations.literal: Gui in youth transmitted Shi's learning; he and his elder brother Yun passed the provincial examination together and both enjoyed contemporary renown.
translations.idiomatic: Gui in youth inherited Shi's learning. He and his elder brother Yun passed the provincial examination together and both enjoyed contemporary renown.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年成進士，年甫十八，選庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi at only eighteen, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and upon release from the Academy was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong (1748) he became a jinshi at only eighteen, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and upon release from the Academy was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 數遇典禮，撰進文冊。

translations.literal: He several times encountered ceremonial occasions and drafted presentation documents.
translations.idiomatic: He several times took part in state ceremonies and drafted presentation documents.

sentences.zh: 高宗重其學行，累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor valued his learning and conduct and repeatedly promoted him to Reader in the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor valued his learning and conduct and repeatedly promoted him to reader in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，出為福建糧驛道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he went out as Fujian grain and courier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year (1760) he was appointed Fujian grain and courier commissioner.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使，治獄平恕，以父憂去。

translations.literal: He was promoted provincial judge, judged cases with fairness and leniency, and left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted provincial judge, judged cases with fairness and leniency, and left office upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，補湖北按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed Hubei provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year (1767) he was appointed Hubei provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 會緬甸用兵，以部署驛務詳慎，被褒獎。

translations.literal: When Burma was at war, because his deployment of courier services was detailed and careful he received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Burma campaign, because his management of courier services was detailed and careful he received commendation.

sentences.zh: 調山西，就遷布政使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shanxi, then promoted provincial administration commissioner and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shanxi, then promoted provincial administration commissioner and acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 疏請歸化、綏遠二城穀二萬餘石搭放兵糧，以省採買、免紅朽；

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that more than twenty thousand shi of grain from the cities of Guihua and Suiyuan be lent for military rations to save purchasing and avoid spoiled grain;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that more than twenty thousand shi of grain from Guihua and Suiyuan be lent for military rations to save purchasing costs and avoid spoiled stores;

sentences.zh: 又免土默特蒙古私墾罪，以所墾牧地三千餘頃，許附近兵民認耕納租，歲六千餘兩，增官兵公費；

translations.literal: he also remitted the crime of unauthorized cultivation by Tumed Mongols, permitting nearby soldiers and civilians to claim and farm more than three thousand qing of pasture land and pay rent of more than six thousand taels yearly to increase official expenses for officers and soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: he also remitted penalties for unauthorized cultivation by Tumed Mongols, permitting nearby soldiers and civilians to claim and farm more than three thousand qing of pasture, paying more than six thousand taels yearly in rent to increase official funds for troops;

sentences.zh: 又太僕寺牧地苦寒，改徵折色，以便民除弊；

translations.literal: and because the Imperial Stud pastures were bitterly cold, he changed collection to cash payment to benefit the people and remove abuses;
translations.idiomatic: and because Imperial Stud pastures were bitterly cold, he changed collection to cash payment to ease the people and remove abuses;

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 珪方正，為同僚所不便，按察使黃檢奏劾讀書廢事。

translations.literal: Gui was upright and inconvenient to colleagues; Provincial Judge Huang Jian memorialized accusing him of neglecting duties through reading.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was upright and inconvenient to colleagues. Provincial Judge Huang Jian memorialized accusing him of neglecting duties through excessive reading.

sentences.zh: 四十年，召入覲，改授侍講學士，直上書房，侍仁宗學。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was summoned to audience, changed to Reader in the Academy, entered the Upper Study directly, and attended the Renzong Emperor's studies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year (1775) he was summoned to audience, appointed reader in the Academy, entered the Upper Study directly, and tutored the Jiaqing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，典福建鄉試。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he presided over the Fujian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year (1779) he presided over the Fujian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 次年，督福建學政。

translations.literal: The following year he supervised Fujian education.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he supervised Fujian education.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，上五箴於仁宗：曰養心，曰敬身，曰勤業，曰虛己，曰致誠。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he presented five admonitions to the Renzong Emperor: cultivate the mind, respect the person, be diligent in duty, empty the self, and achieve sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure he presented five admonitions to the Jiaqing Emperor: cultivate the mind, respect the person, be diligent in duty, empty the self, and achieve sincerity.

sentences.zh: 仁宗力行之，後親政，嘗置左右。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor strove to practice them; after he took power personally he often kept them at hand.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor strove to practice them; after he took personal power he often kept them at hand.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，擢禮部侍郎，典江南鄉試，督浙江學政。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was promoted Vice Minister of Rites, presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination, and supervised Zhejiang education.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year (1786) he was promoted vice minister of rites, presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination, and supervised Zhejiang education.

sentences.zh: 還朝，調兵部。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year (1790) he presided over the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 出為安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: He went out as Anhui governor.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 皖北水災，馳驛往賑，攜僕數人，與村民同舟渡，賑宿州、泗州、碭山、靈壁、五河、盱眙餘災，輕者貸以糧種。

translations.literal: Northern Anhui suffered flood disaster; he traveled post-haste to give relief, taking only a few servants and crossing in the same boat with villagers; he relieved remaining disaster in Suzhou, Sizhou, Dangshan, Lingbi, Wuhe, and Xuyi, and for lighter cases lent grain seed.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Anhui suffered floods. He traveled post-haste to give relief with only a few servants, crossing in the same boats as villagers. He relieved remaining disaster in Suzhou, Sizhou, Dangshan, Lingbi, Wuhe, and Xuyi, and for lighter cases lent grain seed.

sentences.zh: 築決堤，展春賑，並躬蒞其事，民無流亡。

translations.literal: He repaired breached dikes, extended spring relief, and personally oversaw the work; the people did not flee.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired breached dikes, extended spring relief, and personally oversaw the work, so that the people did not flee.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year (1794) he was transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋署兩廣總督，授左都御史、兵部尚書，仍留巡撫任。

translations.literal: Soon he acted as governor-general of Liangguang, was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left and Minister of War, while still retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he acted as governor-general of Liangguang, was appointed left censor-in-chief and minister of war, while still retaining the governorship.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，授總督，兼署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was appointed governor-general while still acting as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing (1796) he was appointed governor-general while still acting as governor.

sentences.zh: 珪初以文學受知，洎出任疆寄，負時望，將大用。

translations.literal: Gui at first won notice through literary accomplishment; when he went out to frontier duty he bore contemporary hopes and was about to be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui at first won notice through literary accomplishment. When he went out to frontier duty he bore great contemporary hopes and was about to receive major appointment.

sentences.zh: 和珅忌之，授受禮成，珪進頌冊，因加指摘，高宗曰：「陳善納誨，師傅之職宜爾，非汝所知也。

translations.literal: Heshen envied him; when the succession ceremony was completed Gui presented a eulogy document and was accordingly criticized; the Gaozong Emperor said: "To present good counsel and accept remonstrance is the tutor's proper duty—not something you would understand.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen envied him. When the succession ceremony was completed Gui presented a eulogy and was criticized for it. The Qianlong Emperor said, "To present good counsel and accept remonstrance is the tutor's proper duty—not something you would understand.

sentences.zh: 」會大學士缺，詔召珪，卒為和珅所沮。

translations.literal: " When a grand secretary post fell vacant an edict summoned Gui, but in the end Heshen obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: " When a grand secretary post fell vacant an edict summoned Gui, but Heshen obstructed it in the end.

sentences.zh: 以廣東艇匪擾劫閩、浙，責珪不能緝捕，寢前命，左遷安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Because Guangdong fast-boat pirates harassed and plundered Fujian and Zhejiang, Gui was blamed for failure to capture them; the previous order was suspended and he was demoted to Anhui governor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Guangdong fast-boat pirates harassed Fujian and Zhejiang, Gui was blamed for failure to capture them. The previous appointment was suspended and he was demoted to Anhui governor.

sentences.zh: 皖北复災，親治賑，官吏無侵蝕。

translations.literal: Northern Anhui suffered disaster again; he personally managed relief and officials did not embezzle.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Anhui suffered disaster again. He personally managed relief and officials did not embezzle.

sentences.zh: 三省教匪起，安徽亦多伏莽。

translations.literal: Sect rebels rose in three provinces and Anhui also had many hidden malcontents.
translations.idiomatic: Sect rebels rose in three provinces, and Anhui also had many hidden malcontents.

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「疑而索之，是激之變。

translations.literal: Gui said: "To suspect and search for them is to provoke rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "To suspect and search for them is to provoke rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」親駐界上籌防禦，遍蒞潁、亳所屬，集鄉老教誡之，民感化，境內迄無事。

translations.literal: " He personally stationed on the border to plan defense, went everywhere in Ying and Bo jurisdictions, gathered village elders to admonish them, and the people were transformed; within the borders there was ultimately no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: " He personally stationed on the border to plan defense, went everywhere in the Ying and Bo jurisdictions, gathered village elders to admonish them, and the people were transformed; within the borders there was ultimately no trouble.

sentences.zh: 明年，授兵部尚書，調吏部，仍留巡撫任。

translations.literal: The following year he was appointed Minister of War, transferred to Personnel, while still retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed minister of war, transferred to personnel, while still retaining the governorship.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，高宗崩，仁宗即馳驛召珪，聞命奔赴。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the Gaozong Emperor died; the Renzong Emperor immediately sent post-horses to summon Gui, who upon hearing the order rushed to obey.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year (1799) the Qianlong Emperor died. The Jiaqing Emperor immediately sent post-horses to summon Gui, who upon hearing the order rushed to obey.

sentences.zh: 途中上疏，略曰：「天子之孝，以繼志述事為大。

translations.literal: On the way he memorialized, saying in summary: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety lies chiefly in continuing the will and carrying forward the work.
translations.idiomatic: On the way he memorialized, saying in summary, "The Son of Heaven's filial piety lies chiefly in continuing his predecessor's will and carrying forward his work.

sentences.zh: 親政伊始，遠聽近瞻，默運乾綱，雱施渙號。

translations.literal: At the beginning of personal rule, listen far and look near, silently wield the heavenly regalia, and broadly dispense edicts of grace.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of personal rule, listen far and look near, silently wield imperial authority, and broadly dispense edicts of grace.

sentences.zh: 陽剛之氣，如日重光，惻怛之仁，無幽不浹。

translations.literal: The yang and firm spirit, like the sun's doubled light; compassionate benevolence penetrating even the hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Let yang firmness shine like the sun at its zenith; let compassionate benevolence penetrate even the hidden.

sentences.zh: 修身則嚴誠欺之界，觀人則辨義利之防。

translations.literal: In self-cultivation draw a strict line against deceit; in observing men distinguish the barrier between righteousness and profit.
translations.idiomatic: In self-cultivation draw a strict line against deceit; in observing men distinguish the barrier between righteousness and profit.

sentences.zh: 君心正而四維張，朝廷清而九牧肅。

translations.literal: When the ruler's mind is correct the four bonds are stretched; when the court is pure the nine provinces are disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler's mind is correct the four bonds of society hold firm; when the court is pure the nine provinces are disciplined.

sentences.zh: 身先節儉，崇獎清廉，自然盜賊不足平，財用不足阜。

translations.literal: Take the lead in frugality and honor integrity—then naturally bandits need not be fully suppressed and resources need not be fully enriched.
translations.idiomatic: Take the lead in frugality and honor integrity—then bandits will subside and resources will grow of themselves.

sentences.zh: 惟原皇上無忘堯、舜自​​任之心，臣敢不勉行義事君之道。

translations.literal: Only pray that Your Majesty not forget the heart that takes Yao and Shun upon itself; your subject dares not fail to strive to practice righteousness in serving the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Only pray that Your Majesty not forget the heart that takes Yao and Shun upon itself; your servant dares not fail to strive to practice righteousness in serving the ruler.

sentences.zh: 」至京哭臨，上執珪手哭失聲。

translations.literal: " When he reached the capital for mourning rites the emperor took Gui's hand and wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: " When he reached the capital for mourning rites the emperor took Gui's hand and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 命直南書房，管戶部三庫，加太子少保，賜第西華門外。

translations.literal: He was ordered to attend the Southern Study, manage the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted a residence outside Xihua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to the Southern Study, to manage the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, given the additional title of junior guardian of the heir apparent, and granted a residence outside Xihua Gate.

sentences.zh: 時召獨對，用人行政悉以諮之。

translations.literal: He was then summoned for private audiences; employment and administration were all consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was then summoned for private audiences; appointments and administration were all consulted with him.

sentences.zh: 珪造膝密陳，不關白軍機大臣，不沽恩市直，上傾心一聽，初政之美，多出贊助。

translations.literal: Gui spoke confidentially at the emperor's knee, did not inform the Grand Council members, and did not curry favor with blunt honesty; the emperor listened with full trust—the beauty of the early reign owed much to his assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Gui spoke confidentially at the emperor's knee, did not inform the grand councilors, and did not curry favor with blunt honesty. The emperor listened with full trust—the beauty of the early reign owed much to his assistance.

sentences.zh: 尋充上書房總師傅，調戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he served as Chief Tutor of the Upper Study and was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as chief tutor of the Upper Study and was transferred to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 詔清漕政，禁浮收​​。

translations.literal: An edict ordered purification of grain transport administration and prohibition of excessive collection.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered purification of grain transport administration and prohibition of excessive collection.

sentences.zh: 疆吏以運丁苦累，仰給州縣，州縣不得不取諸民，於是安徽加贈銀，江蘇加耗米，珪謂小民未見清漕之益，先受其害，力爭罷之，令曹司凡事近加賦者皆議駁。

translations.literal: Border officials said transport laborers were burdened and depended on districts and counties, which had to take from the people; thus Anhui added supplementary silver and Jiangsu added surplus grain. Gui said the common people had not yet seen the benefit of purified transport but first suffered harm; he contended vigorously to abolish this and ordered all offices that anything approaching added levies must be deliberated and rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials said transport laborers were overburdened and depended on districts and counties, which had to take from the people; thus Anhui added supplementary silver and Jiangsu added surplus grain. Gui said the common people had not yet seen the benefit of purified transport but already suffered harm. He contended vigorously to abolish these measures and ordered that anything approaching added levies must be deliberated and rejected.

sentences.zh: 長蘆鹽政請加增鹽價，駁曰：「蘆東因錢價賤，已三加價矣，且免積欠三百六十萬兩，餘欠展三年，商力已寬，無庸再議加價。

translations.literal: The Changlu salt administration requested increased salt price; he rejected it, saying: "In eastern Hebei, because money was cheap, price has already been raised three times, and more than 3.6 million taels of arrears were remitted with the remainder spread over three years—merchant capacity is already eased; there is no need to discuss raising price again.
translations.idiomatic: The Changlu salt administration requested an increased salt price. He rejected it, saying, "In eastern Hebei, because money was cheap, the price has already been raised three times, and more than 3.6 million taels of arrears were remitted with the remainder spread over three years. Merchant capacity is already eased; there is no need to raise the price again.

sentences.zh: 」廣東請濱海沙地升賦，駁曰：「海沙淤地，坍漲靡常，故照下則減半賦之。

translations.literal: " Guangdong requested raising assessments on coastal sand land; he rejected it, saying: "Sea sand silt land shifts with erosion and accretion and is therefore assessed at half the lowest rate.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangdong requested raising assessments on coastal sand land. He rejected it, saying, "Sea-silt land shifts with erosion and accretion and is therefore assessed at half the lowest rate.

sentences.zh: 今視上、中田增賦，是與民計微利，非政體。

translations.literal: Now to assess it like upper and middle fields is to wring petty profit from the people—not proper governance.
translations.idiomatic: Now to assess it like upper and middle fields is to wring petty profit from the people—not proper governance.

sentences.zh: 且民苦加賦，別有漲地，將不敢報墾，不可行。

translations.literal: Moreover, the people suffer from added levies; if there is reclaimed land they will not dare report cultivation—this cannot be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the people already suffer from added levies; if there is newly reclaimed land they will not dare report it—this cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 」倉場請預納錢糧四五十倍，準作義監生，駁曰：「國家正供有常經，名實關體要。

translations.literal: " The granary office requested prepayment of grain tax forty or fifty times over to qualify as charitable tribute student; he rejected it, saying: "The state's regular tribute has fixed rules; name and reality concern the body politic.
translations.idiomatic: " The granary office requested prepayment of grain tax forty or fifty times over to qualify as charitable tribute student. He rejected it, saying, "The state's regular revenue has fixed rules; name and reality concern the body politic.

sentences.zh: 於名不正，實必傷，斷不可行。

translations.literal: If the name is not correct, the substance must be harmed—this absolutely cannot be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: If the name is not correct, the substance must be harmed—this absolutely cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 」凡駁議每自屬稿，奏上，皆韙之。

translations.literal: " Whenever he drafted rejections himself and submitted them, all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever he drafted rejections himself and submitted them, the emperor approved them all.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he concurrently acted as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1800) he concurrently acted as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 先是彭元瑞於西華門內墜馬，珪呼其輿入舁之，為御史週栻所劾。

translations.literal: Earlier Peng Yuanrui fell from his horse inside Xihua Gate; Gui called his sedan in to carry him and was impeached by Censor Zhou Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Peng Yuanrui fell from his horse inside Xihua Gate. Gui called his sedan in to carry him and was impeached by Censor Zhou Shi.

sentences.zh: 尋有珪輿人毆傷禁門兵，忌者嗾護軍統領訐之。

translations.literal: Soon Gui's sedan bearers beat and injured a Forbidden Gate guard; enemies incited the guard commander to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gui's sedan bearers beat and injured a Forbidden Gate guard; enemies incited the guard commander to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 詔：「珪素恪謹，造次不檢，特申戒。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Gui is by nature careful and respectful; in a moment of carelessness he was not restrained—he is specially admonished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Gui is by nature careful and respectful; in a moment of carelessness he was unrestrained—he is specially admonished.

sentences.zh: 」坐褫宮銜，解三庫事，鐫級留任。

translations.literal: " He was punished by stripping palace rank, relieved of the three treasuries, reduced in grade but retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: " He was punished by stripping palace rank, relieved of the three treasuries, reduced in grade but retained in office.

sentences.zh: 七年，協辦大學士，复太子少保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he served as Associate Grand Secretary and was restored to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1802) he served as associate grand secretary and was restored to junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋兼翰林院掌院學士，晉太子少傅。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and was advanced to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and was advanced to junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 九年，上幸翰林院，聯句賜宴，御書「天祿儲才」額刻懸院中，以墨書賜珪家。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the emperor visited the Hanlin Academy, joined in verse at a banquet, and in imperial calligraphy wrote the plaque "Heaven's Blessing Stores Talent" to be carved and hung in the academy, and gave the ink writing to Gui's family.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1804) the emperor visited the Hanlin Academy, joined in verse at a banquet, and in imperial calligraphy wrote the plaque "Heaven's Blessing Stores Talent" to be carved and hung in the academy, and gave the ink writing to Gui's family.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜體仁閣大學士，管理工部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Cherishing Humanity and placed in charge of the Ministry of Works.
