translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1805) he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Cherishing Humanity and placed in charge of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 上以是命遵高宗諭，遣詣裕陵謝。

translations.literal: Because this appointment followed the Gaozong Emperor's instruction, he was sent to offer thanks at the Yuling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Because this appointment followed the Qianlong Emperor's instruction, he was sent to offer thanks at the Yuling Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，年七十六，以老乞休，溫詔慰留，賜玉鳩杖；

translations.literal: After more than a year, at age seventy-six, he begged to retire on account of age; a warm edict comforted him and kept him, granting a jade dove staff;
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, at age seventy-six, he begged to retire on account of age. A warm edict urged him to stay and granted him a jade dove staff;

sentences.zh: 命天寒，間二三日入直。

translations.literal: he was ordered that in cold weather he need attend duty only every two or three days.
translations.idiomatic: he was ordered that in cold weather he need attend duty only every two or three days.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召對乾清宮，眩暈，扶歸第，數日卒。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to audience in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, grew dizzy, was helped back to his residence, and died within several days.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to audience in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, grew dizzy, was helped back to his residence, and died within several days.

sentences.zh: 上親奠，哭之慟。

translations.literal: The emperor personally offered libations and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally offered libations and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，祀賢良祠，賜金治喪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and given gold for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed grand tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Ministers, and granted gold for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 詔：「珪自為師傅，凡所陳說，無非唐、虞、三代之言，稍涉時趨者不出諸口，啟沃至多。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Since Gui became tutor, whatever he stated was nothing but the words of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties; anything touching current fashion never passed his lips—his secret counsel was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Since Gui became tutor, whatever he stated was nothing but the words of the sage-kings of antiquity; anything touching current fashion never passed his lips—his secret counsel was abundant.

sentences.zh: 揆諸諡法，足當'正'字而無愧，特諡文正。

translations.literal: Measured against posthumous title standards, he fully merits the character 'correct' without shame—he is specially given the posthumous title Wénzhèng.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against posthumous title standards, he fully merits the character for 'correct' without shame—he is specially given the posthumous title Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 又見其門庭卑隘，清寒之況，不減儒素。

translations.literal: Moreover, seeing his gate and courtyard low and narrow, his condition of clean poverty did not fall short of a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, seeing his gate and courtyard low and narrow, his condition of clean poverty did not fall short of a poor scholar's.

sentences.zh: 」命內府備筵，遣皇子加奠。

translations.literal: " He ordered the inner palace to prepare a feast and sent a prince to offer additional libations.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the inner palace to prepare a feast and sent a prince to offer additional libations.

sentences.zh: 啟殯日，遣慶郡王永璘祖奠目送。

translations.literal: On the day the coffin was opened he sent Prince Yonglin of Qing to offer ancestral libations and see him off.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the coffin was opened he sent Prince Yonglin of Qing to offer ancestral libations and see him off.

sentences.zh: 逾年，上謁西陵，珪墓近蹕路，遣官賜奠。

translations.literal: After more than a year the emperor visited the Western Tombs; Gui's tomb was near the imperial route and an official was sent to grant libations.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the emperor visited the Western Tombs. Gui's tomb lay near the imperial route and an official was sent to grant libations.

sentences.zh: 高宗實錄成，特賜祭，擢長子錫經為四品京堂。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor's Veritable Records were completed he was specially granted sacrifice and his eldest son Xijing was promoted to fourth-rank capital bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor's Veritable Records were completed he was specially granted sacrifice and his eldest son Xijing was promoted to fourth-rank capital bureau director.

sentences.zh: 二十年，復因謁陵回鑾，親奠其墓，恩禮始終無與比。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, again on returning from tomb visitation, he personally offered libations at the tomb—favor from start to finish was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1815), again on returning from tomb visitation, he personally offered libations at the tomb—favor from start to finish was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 珪文章奧博，取士重經策，銳意求才。

translations.literal: Gui's literary compositions were profound and broad; in selecting scholars he valued classical examinations and keenly sought talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's literary compositions were profound and broad. In selecting scholars he valued classical examinations and keenly sought talent.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年典會試，阮元佐之，一時名流搜拔殆盡，為士林宗仰者數十年。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he presided over the metropolitan examination with Ruan Yuan assisting; the leading figures of the age were nearly all selected and for decades were revered by the scholarly community.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing (1799) he presided over the metropolitan examination with Ruan Yuan assisting. The leading figures of the age were nearly all selected and for decades were revered by the scholarly community.

sentences.zh: 學無不通，亦喜道家，嘗曰：「硃子注參同契，非空言也。

translations.literal: His learning had no field he did not master; he also delighted in Daoism and once said: "Zhu Xi's commentary on the Cantong qi is not empty words.
translations.idiomatic: His learning had no field he did not master. He also delighted in Daoism and once said, "Zhu Xi's commentary on the Cantong qi is not empty words.

sentences.zh: 論曰：君子小人消長之機，國運系焉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The mechanism by which the gentleman and the petty man wax and wane—the nation's fate depends on it.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: The mechanism by which gentlemen and petty men wax and wane—the nation's fate depends on it.

sentences.zh: 王杰、董誥、硃珪皆高宗拔擢信任之臣，和珅一再間沮，卒不屈撓。

translations.literal: Wang Jie, Dong Gao, and Zhu Gui were all ministers the Gaozong Emperor selected and trusted; Heshen repeatedly obstructed them between, yet in the end they did not yield or bend.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie, Dong Gao, and Zhu Gui were all ministers the Qianlong Emperor selected and trusted. Heshen repeatedly obstructed them, yet in the end they did not yield.

sentences.zh: 一旦共、驩伏法，眾正盈朝，攄其忠誠，啟沃新主，殄寇息民，苞桑永固。

translations.literal: Once Gong and Huan were executed by law, the upright filled the court; they poured forth loyalty, secretly counseled the new ruler, exterminated bandits and gave the people rest—the nation was firmly secured like a triple-rooted mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: Once Heshen and his faction were executed, the upright filled the court. They poured forth loyalty, secretly counseled the new ruler, exterminated bandits and gave the people rest—the nation was firmly secured.

sentences.zh: 天留數人，弼成仁宗初政之盛，可謂大臣矣。

translations.literal: Heaven left a few such men to assist and complete the splendor of the Renzong Emperor's early reign—they may truly be called great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven left a few such men to assist and complete the splendor of the Jiaqing Emperor's early reign—they may truly be called great ministers.
